literature_notes: CD151 is a tetraspanin with a type III topology: both the N-terminus (residues 1–17) and the C-terminus (residues 243–253) are intracellular. The only extracellular-facing regions are the small extracellular loop (SEL, residues 44–58) and the large extracellular loop (LEL, residues 114–221), neither of which is a terminus. All five ledger lines (L1–L5) describe GFP-tagged CD151 expressed in BJAB cells, but none qualifies as a surface tag site for the following reasons: (1) No ledger line names a residue, junction, or loop in an extracellular span as the GFP insertion point. (2) The flow-cytometry readouts in L1–L3 and L5 confirm CD151 surface expression via anti-CD151 antibody, not GFP surface display — GFP fluorescence and anti-GFP nanobody pulldown (L2) are both compatible with an intracellular GFP tag. (3) L4 describes commercial GenScript plasmids with N- and C-terminally tagged CD151; this is excluded by the rule against commercial plasmids with unstated tag positions, and in any case both termini of CD151 are intracellular. (4) The 'topology_derived' rule requires exactly one extracellular terminus; CD151 has zero extracellular termini, so it cannot be applied. The GFP tag in L1–L3 and L5 is most plausibly at the intracellular C-terminus (standard practice for tetraspanins), recorded in other_positions.

literature_other_positions.note: L4 explicitly mentions C-terminally tagged CD151 purchased from GenScript; the C-terminus (residues 243–253) is intracellular per topology landmarks, so any tag appended after residue 253 faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular space.
L4 also mentions N-terminally tagged CD151; the N-terminus (residues 1–17) is intracellular per topology landmarks, so a tag prepended before residue 1 also faces the cytoplasm.
